chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Iblis (may Allah curse him) disputed with Noah (peace be upon him) regarding the vineyard. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'Indeed, he has a right, so give it to him.' So he gave him one-third. But Iblis did not agree. Then he gave him one-half, but he did not agree. So Gabriel threw fire, and it burned the two-thirds, and the one-third remained. So he said: 'Whatever the fire burned, that is his share, and whatever remains, that is permissible for you, O Noah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the prohibition of wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the primordial origin of wine (*khamr*) through a divine negotiation between Iblis and Prophet Noah (AS), where fire serves as the arbiter to determine ownership shares. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narrative is often interpreted to explain the specific 'share' of Iblis in the fruit of the vine, linking the physical property of grapes to spiritual corruption, while establishing the remaining portion as halal for human consumption.
